thighLift.heroDesc1: A thigh lift, medically known as thighplasty, is a surgical procedure designed to remove excess skin and fat from the thighs to restore a firmer, smoother, and more proportionate contour. It is most commonly considered after significant weight loss, ageing, or genetic skin laxity—situations where the thigh skin loses elasticity and fails to retract, even with regular exercise.
thighLift.heroDesc2: This procedure is intended for individuals who are close to a stable, healthy weight but are left with sagging inner or outer thigh skin that causes friction, discomfort in clothing, or dissatisfaction with body proportions. When performed correctly, a thigh lift improves both appearance and daily comfort, particularly during walking and physical activity.
thighLift.heroDesc3: In Malaysia, thigh lift surgery is classified as a regulated surgical procedure. It must be performed by a registered medical practitioner in a licensed healthcare facility under standards governed by the Ministry of Health Malaysia (MOH), which oversees private healthcare services, surgical safety, and professional accountability.
thighLift.whatDesc: A thigh lift is a surgical procedure that removes excess skin and, when necessary, underlying fat from the thighs. The goal is to reshape the thighs by tightening loose tissue and improving overall contour and skin smoothness. It is not a weight-loss surgery but a contour-restoring procedure for patients whose skin can no longer tighten naturally.
thighLift.causesDesc: The thighs are especially prone to sagging because the skin in this area is thin, mobile, and affected by constant movement. Once skin elasticity is lost, exercise can improve muscle tone but cannot eliminate excess skin.
thighLift.typesDesc: The appropriate thigh lift technique is chosen after a detailed clinical assessment based on anatomy, skin quality, and aesthetic goals.
thighLift.type1Desc: Targets sagging skin along the inner thighs. Incision placed in the groin crease or extending downward.
thighLift.type2Desc: Addresses laxity of the outer thighs and hips. Incision typically concealed within the waistline.
thighLift.type3Desc: Suitable for mild upper inner-thigh laxity. Smaller incision with limited skin removal.
thighLift.type4Desc: Corrects extensive laxity extending toward the knee. Often chosen after massive weight loss.
thighLift.benefitsDesc: For suitable candidates, a thigh lift offers both aesthetic and functional benefits. Patients often report improved confidence and physical comfort in daily activities.
thighLift.benefit1Desc: Eliminates sagging thigh skin that doesn't respond to exercise.
thighLift.benefit3Desc: Eliminates chafing during walking and physical activity.
thighLift.benefit4Desc: Improves comfort in fitted clothing and swimwear.
thighLift.benefit5Desc: Balances body contours after weight loss.
thighLift.benefit6Desc: Permanent improvement when weight remains stable.
thighLift.floatingBadgeDesc: Results are permanent as long as weight remains stable and healthy habits are maintained.
thighLift.notRecNote: Final suitability is confirmed during an in-person consultation and physical examination.
thighLift.compareNote: In cases of poor skin elasticity, liposuction alone may worsen sagging.
thighLift.recoveryDesc: Thigh lift results develop progressively as swelling resolves and tissues heal.
thighLift.resPoint4b: Scars continue to mature and fade
thighLift.scarDesc: Scarring is an unavoidable aspect of thigh lift surgery, but careful planning minimizes visibility. Realistic expectations regarding scars are an essential part of preoperative counselling.
thighLift.scarItem1Desc: Scars are placed in natural creases when possible.
thighLift.scarItem3Desc: Wound care and sun protection improve scar quality.
thighLift.scarItem4Desc: Final appearance depends on skin type and healing response.
thighLift.scarFadeDesc: Initial scars may appear red or pink but typically fade significantly over 6–12 months, becoming flat and lighter in colour.
thighLift.aftercare1Desc: Worn for 4–6 weeks to support healing

thighLift.faqDesc: Get answers to common concerns about thigh lift surgery
thighLift.faq1A: A thigh lift is a surgical procedure that removes excess skin and fat from the thighs to improve firmness and contour.
thighLift.faq2Q: Is a thigh lift the same as thigh liposuction?
thighLift.faq2A: No. Liposuction removes fat only, while a thigh lift removes loose skin and reshapes the thighs.
thighLift.faq3A: When performed by a certified plastic surgeon in a regulated facility, it is considered a safe and established procedure.
thighLift.faq4Q: How long does recovery take after a thigh lift?
thighLift.faq4A: Most patients resume daily activities within 2–4 weeks, with full recovery over several months.
thighLift.faq5A: Yes, but scars are placed strategically and fade over time with proper care.
thighLift.faq6A: Results are long-lasting if body weight remains stable.
thighLift.faq7Q: Can a thigh lift be combined with other procedures?
thighLift.faq7A: Yes. It is often combined with tummy tuck or body lift surgery after weight loss.
thighLift.faq8Q: Does exercise help after a thigh lift?
thighLift.faq8A: Exercise improves muscle tone but cannot replace surgical skin removal.
thighLift.faq9Q: Who should consider a thigh lift?
thighLift.faq9A: Patients with loose thigh skin after weight loss or ageing and stable weight.
thighLift.faq10A: Overall health and skin condition are more important than age alone.
thighLift.safety1Desc: Thigh lift surgery is regulated under the Private Healthcare Services framework, ensuring surgical safety and professional accountability.
thighLift.safety2Desc: All procedures are performed in accredited, licensed medical facilities with full monitoring protocols.
thighLift.safety3Desc: Dr. Soma is a registered medical practitioner and specialist plastic surgeon with experience in body contouring surgery.
thighLift.ctaDesc: A thigh lift is about restoring comfort, proportion, and confidence. Dr. Soma delivers personalised solutions with surgical precision and structured postoperative care.
